Proof of Claim (Official Form 410)
 Read the instructions before filling out this form. This form is for making a claim for payment in a bankruptcy case. With the exception of 503(b)(9),
 do not use this form to make a request for payment of an administrative expense. Make such a request according to 11 U.S.C. § 503.
 Filers must leave out or redact information that is entitled to privacy on this form or on any attached documents. Attach redacted copies of any
 documents that support the claim, such as promissory notes, purchase orders, invoices, itemized statements of running accounts, contracts, judgments,
 mortgages, and security agreements. Do not send original documents; they may be destroyed after scanning. If the documents are not available,
 explain in an attachment.
 A person who files a fraudulent claim could be fined up to $500,000, imprisoned for up to 5 years, or both. 18 U.S.C. §§ 152, 157, and 3571.
 Fill in all the information about the claim as of the date the case was filed. That date is on the notice of bankruptcy (Form 309) that you received.

under 503(b)(9), do not use this form to make a request for payment of an administrative expense. Make such a request according to 11 U.S.C. § 503.

mortgages, and security agreements. Do not send original documents; they may be destroyed after scanning. If the documents are not available,
explain in an attachment.

                ADDENDUM TO PROOF OF CLAIM – LTL CONTRACT

      Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. (“Claimant”), in its own capacity submits this addendum (the
“Addendum”) to its proof of claim (“Proof of Claim”) against YRC Inc. (Case No. 23-11087),
USF Holland LLC (Case No. 23-11079), USF Reddaway Inc. (Case No. 23-11081); and New
Penn Motor Express LLC (Case No. 23-11072) (“Debtor(s)”), and respectfully states as follows:

                                       Bankruptcy Filing

        1.    On August 6, 2023 (“Petition Date”), the Debtors and certain other affiliates
commenced voluntary cases (“Case”) under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code with the United
States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware (“Court”).

       2.      On September 13, 2023, the Court entered that certain Final Order (I) Authorizing
the Debtors to Consent to Limited Relief From the Automatic Stay to Permit Setoff of Certain
Customer Claims Against the Debtors, and (II) Granting Related Relief [Dkt. No. 522] pursuant
to which Debtors are authorized to honor any undisputed prepetition obligations related to the
Customer Programs in the ordinary course through the execution of setoff agreements.

                                        Basis for Claim

        3.      On November 7, 2020, Claimant and Debtors entered into a Master Logistics
Services Agreement - LTL (“LTL”) for logistics services to be provided by Debtors to Claimant
which was amended on: (a) September 22, 2021 pursuant to that certain Schedule A-4 Ocean
Pricing (“Schedule A-4”); (b) September 24, 2021 pursuant to that certain Schedule A-2
Guaranteed Delivery Service (“Schedule A-2”); (c) October 27, 2022 pursuant to that certain
Statement of Work for Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) Transportation (“SOW”); (d) November 27,
2022 pursuant to that certain Amendment to For Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) Transportation
(“First Amendment”); (e) November 27, 2022 pursuant to that certain Amendment to For Less-
Than-Truckload (LTL) Transportation (“Second Amendment”); (f) December 5, 2022 pursuant
to that certain Amendment to For Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) Transportation (“Third
Amendment”); and (g) February 24, 2023, pursuant to that certain Amendment to For Less-
Than-Truckload (LTL) Transportation (“Fourth Amendment” and collectively with the Schedule
A-4, Schedule A-2, SOW, First Amendment, Second Amendment, and Third Amendment, the
“Agreement,” which documents are attached here as Group Exhibit A).

       4.     Under the Agreement, Debtors contracted to provide logistics services for
Claimant including the safe, timely, and careful transportation of goods on behalf of Claimant to
Claimant’s customers or to other destinations as required by Claimant. Pursuant to Section 3 of
the Agreement, each shipment is to be evidenced by a bill of lading.

       5.      Based on notice that Claimant received from Debtors regarding the announced
union workers’ strike, Debtors ceased new freight pickups from Claimant on or about July 18,
2023. Based on Debtors’ cessation of operations, Claimant began rescuing stranded freight from
Debtors on or about July 30, 2023.

        6.     Pursuant to Section 5 of the Agreement, Debtors are liable to Claimant for the
loss of, or damage to, products in accordance with 49 U.S.C. Section 14706. Debtors’ liability

                                                1
commences upon their receipt of each shipment and terminates upon delivery of the shipment to
the consignee in accordance with the governing bill of lading. See Agreement, § 5(A). Debtors
are also liable to Claimant for any shipment, or any part thereof, that is lost, damaged, or
destroyed while under the care, custody, and/or control of Debtors such that Debtors are required
to pay Claimant the replacement cost of the products lost, damaged, or destroyed. Id. at § 5(B).
Further, in the event that Debtors fail to complete any transportation undertaken by it or if any
party with whom Claimant contracts completes such transportation, Debtors shall be responsible
for reasonable and necessary actual costs, charges, fees and expenses incurred by Claimant and
related thereto. Id., § 5(F).

         7.     To the extent that Claimant prevails in litigation against Debtors, then Claimant
shall be entitled to recover all of its actual costs and expenses incurred, including reasonable
attorney’s fees, court costs and interest due as of the scheduled date of delivery of the products.
Id., § 5(M).

        8.     Claimant asserts a claim in the amount of at least $16,496,493.54 based on
Claimant’s damages under the Agreement. Claimant’s damages under the Agreement consist of
the following:

                                           Recoupment and Setoff

        9.      Section 7(C) of the Agreement provides that Claimant “shall have the right to
offset against amounts owed to [Debtor] any amounts due to [Claimant] for claims of loss or
damage, as described in Section 5 of this Agreement.” Further, Bankruptcy Code Section 553
provides that “this title does not affect any right of a creditor to offset a mutual debt owning by
such creditor to the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case … against a claim of
such creditor against the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case.” In addition,
while “[t]he Bankruptcy Code does not contain a recoupment provision, [ ] the right is preserved
through established common law.” In re FormTech Inds., LLC, 439 B.R. 352, 362 (Bankr.
D.Del. 2010) (citing Univ. Med. Ctr. v. Sullivan (In re Univ. Med. Ctr.), 973 F.2d 1065, 1079 (3d
Cir. 1992).

       10.    Claimant is in receipt of documents, including invoices, from Debtors seeking
$10,038,113.28 for logistics services allegedly provided to Claimant prior to the Petition Date.8

        11.    Accordingly, Claimant asserts that it is entitled to recoup and/or setoff the entirety
of its damages under the Agreement (as set forth above) against Debtors’ claims.

        12.      Under Third Circuit case law, the doctrine of recoupment “allows the creditor to
assert that certain mutual claims extinguish one another in bankruptcy.” Lee v. Schweiker, 739
F.2d 870, 875 (3d Cir. 1984). The justification for the recoupment doctrine is that where the
creditor’s claim against the debtor arises from the same transaction as the debtor’s claim, it is
essentially a defense to the debtor’s claim against the creditor rather than a mutual obligation.”
Id. The Third Circuit holds that corresponding liabilities arising under a single contract are

6
  See Note 1, supra.
7
  See Note 1, supra.
8
  Claimant reserves all rights to dispute any or all of the invoices submitted by Debtors to Claimant. Claimant and
Debtors are also party to a separate Master Logistics Agreement dated as October 9, 2016.

                                                          4
subject to the doctrine to recoupment. In re Flagstaff Realty Assocs., 60 F.3d 1031, 1035 (3d
Cir. 1995) (permitting recoupment between tenant’s claim for repair costs and landlord’s claim
for rent arising from lease). The automatic stay does not apply to the doctrine of recoupment.
“[U]nlike a creditor seeking a 11 U.S.C. § 553 setoff, a creditor claiming recoupment need not
apply for stay relief, because the funds subject to recoupment are not the debtor’s property.” In
re Mewborn, 367 B.R. 529, 535 (Bankr. D.N.J. 2006). Accordingly, recoupment is not enjoined
by 11 U.S.C. § 362(a).

       13.      For the doctrine of recoupment to apply, the “same transaction” test must be met.
“[B]oth debts must arise out of a single integrated transaction so that it would be inequitable for
the debtor to enjoy the benefits of that transaction without also meeting its obligations.” Id.
With respect to logistics services agreements such as the Agreement, “[r]ecoupment typically
allows a creditor to recoup claims for overpayment, damage-in-transit, and late delivery….”
FormTech Inds., 439 B.R. at 362. In this case, Claimant’s claims against Debtors arise from the
same transactions as Debtors’ alleged claims against Claimant - with of both arise under the
Agreement. Thus, the doctrine of recoupment applies and Claimant may recoup from
outstanding amounts owed to the Debtors such amounts necessary to satisfy its damage claims
under the Agreement.

        14.     Further, Claimant has a right to setoff under 11 U.S.C. § 553. “Setoff, in effect,
elevates an unsecured claim to secured status, to the extent that the debtor has a mutual, pre-
petition claim against the creditor.” Lee v. Schweiker, 739 F.2d 870, 875 (3d Cir. 1984). “The
requisite elements of a Section 553 setoff are: (1) the creditor holds a claim against the debtor
that arose before the commencement of the case; (2) the creditor owes a debt to the debtor that
also arose before the commencement of the case; (3) the claim and debt are mutual; and (4) the
claim and debt are each valid and enforceable.” In re Stienes, 285 B.R. 360, 362 (Bankr. D.N.J.
2002).

        15.     Here, Claimant has a contractual right to setoff under the Agreement. First,
Claimant’s claims against Debtor are valid pre-petition claims. Second, Debtors’ alleged claims
are also pre-petition claims. Third, the claims are mutual. “To be mutual, the debts must be in
the same right and between the same parties, standing in the same capacity.” Matter of Bevill,
Bresler & Schulman Asset Mgmt. Corp., 896 F.2d 54, 59 (3d Cir. 1990). Application of
mutuality, like in Bevil, is straightforward as the Claimant’s claim arises under the Agreement
and Debtors’ claims arise under the Agreement with respect to certain identifiable freight
deliveries. Id. (Mutuality is “straightforward” when claims are based on breach of contract
leading to a “symmetry of obligations.”). Because Claimant’s claim against Debtors and
Debtors’ claims against Claimant relate to the same pre-petition Agreement and invoices, there is
mutuality as required under Section 553 of the Bankruptcy Code. Thus, to the extent Debtors
hold valid pre-petition claims relating to pre-petition invoices, Claimant has a right to setoff its
mutual pre-petition claim relating to the same invoices. See In re Alfar Dairy, Inc., 458 F.2d
1258, 1262 (5th Cir. 1972) (offsetting mutual pre-petition claims).

      16.     Therefore, for the reasons set forth above, Claimant is entitled to withhold
payment under the Agreement and invoices to preserve its future ability to effectuate a
recoupment or setoff with respect to its pre-petition damage claims arising under the Agreement


                                                 5
and invoices. See In re Rooster, Inc., 127 B.R. 560 (Bankr. E.D. Pa. 1991) (seller of fabric to
debtor was entitled, by way of recoupment, to offset from prepayment deposit held by seller).

                                        MASTER LOGISTICS SERVICES AGREEMENT--LTL


            This Master Logistics Services Agreement (the “Master Agreement”) is made and entered into as of November 7,
            2020, (the “Effective Date”) by and between the HOME DEPOT U.S.A., INC., a Delaware corporation, with offices
            at 2455 Paces Ferry Road, Atlanta, Georgia, 30339, on behalf of itself and its affiliates (collectively “The Home
            Depot” or “Shipper”), and YRC Inc. d/b/a YRC Freight, a Delaware corporation; USF Holland LLC, d/b/a Holland,
            a Delaware limited liability company; USF Reddaway Inc. d/b/a Reddaway, an Oregon corporation; and New Penn
            Motor Express LLC, d/b/a New Penn Motor Express a Delaware limited liability (the “YRC Carriers”) (who enter
            into this Master Agreement through their authorized agent, YRC Enterprise Services, Inc., a Delaware corporation), .
            Affiliates may be added or deleted from this Agreement by written agreement of the Parties.


                      For purposes of this Agreement, YRC ESI is solely a negotiating agent for each named Carrier and assumes
            no legal responsibility or liability for performance or obligations under this Agreement. Each YRC Carrier is solely
            responsible for all services such Carrier provides. References herein to “Party” or to the “Parties” shall mean, in the
            case of the YRC Carriers, the actual YRC Carrier providing service to The Home Depot pursuant to this Agreement,
            as may be applicable. References to “Carrier” shall be to the individual YRC Carrier performing the services under
            this Master Agreement or to all of them if the context requires that all YRC Carriers satisfy the stated contractual
            requirement.

                     The Home Depot hereby agrees that with the exception of The Home Depot termination rights under this
            Master Agreement (as detailed below), all legal recourse against a YRC Carrier regarding such Carrier’s services
            herein must be asserted by Customer directly against such individual YRC Carrier and not against YRC ESI.
            Therefore, The Home Depot acknowledges and agrees that each YRC Carrier is individually liable regarding the
            services it performs and there is no joint liability between or among such YRC Carriers or YRC ESI. The Home
            Depot acknowledges and agrees that YRC ESI is not a motor carrier, as defined by Title 49 of the United States
            Code or any other governmental authority/agency. In the event of termination, each YRC Carrier may unilaterally
            exercise its termination rights as provided in the Master Agreement without affecting the applicability of the
            Agreement as between the other YRC Carriers. The Home Depot may exercise its termination rights as provided in
            the Master Agreement against individual YRC Carriers, or against all YRC Carriers, at its option.


                      WHEREAS, The Home Depot desires to engage the services of a logistics company to provide certain
            logistics services for The Home Depot including the safe, timely, and careful transportation of goods (the
            “Products”) on behalf of The Home Depot to The Home Depot’s customers (“Customers”) or to other destinations
            as required by The Home Depot and as set forth and scheduled herein; and

                     WHEREAS, Carrier is a logistics provider registered with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
            (“FMCSA”), (Carrier Number details are as stated on the attached Exhibit C)_, and has indicated a desire to perform
            the Services (as defined below) for The Home Depot in accordance with The Home Depot’s requirements and
            specifications, as set forth in this Agreement (as defined below);

                      NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and promises of The Home Depot and
            Carrier, and other good and valuable consideration, the parties agree as follows:

            1.       Agreement Structure

                     A.        The Services will be described in one or more statements of work (“Statement of Work” or
            “SOW”) executed by The Home Depot and Carrier pursuant to this Master Agreement and are subject to this Master
            Agreement. This Master Agreement and the Statement(s) of Work collectively constitute the “Agreement”. Each
            Statement of Work may include a set of schedules (“Schedules”) described therein, with such additions and
            deletions as the parties may agree. Changes to any SOW shall be made only in writing executed by authorized
            representatives of both parties. If there is any ambiguity, inconsistency or discrepancy between this Master
            Agreement and any SOW, this Master Agreement shall govern.

            2.        Carrier’s Service Obligations

                      A.       “Services” is hereby defined as the services, functions, responsibilities, activities, tasks and
            projects to be performed by Carrier, as set forth in this Agreement, including each Statement of Work, as they may
            evolve and be supplemented and enhanced by mutual agreement during the Term (as defined below). Carrier and
            The Home Depot may also develop continually improving standard operating procedures (“SOPs”) for the Services.
            Carrier and The Home Depot may also agree on performance levels and service quality criteria (“Service Level
            Agreements”) to measure and evaluate Carrier’s performance of the Services. These SOPs and Service Level
            Agreements shall be set forth and made a part of the applicable SOW.

                    B.        Carrier shall render Services using personnel, subcontractors and agents of Carrier (collectively,
            “Representatives”) that have the necessary knowledge, training, skills, experience, qualifications, permits, licenses
            and resources to provide and perform the Services in accordance with the Agreement, and shall render Services in a
            prompt, professional, diligent, workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards applicable to the
            performance of such Services. Carrier’s Representatives shall not engage in unlawful or improper conduct in The
            Home Depot facilities or The Home Depot’s agents’ facilities.

                      C.       Carrier shall perform all administrative and recordkeeping tasks associated with and necessary to
            fully and properly perform the Services under the Agreement including the possession, identification, and tracking
            of all Products under Carrier’s custody and control. In addition, Carrier shall maintain a complete and accurate
            record of every Product tendered to a Representative performing Services, and shall furnish such data to The Home
            Depot on a weekly basis, in a form and format specified by The Home Depot, and otherwise upon request, free of
            charge, in order to facilitate The Home Depot’s tracking of Products. Carrier shall permit The Home Depot to audit
            such records during normal Carrier business hours at a time scheduled with Carrier.

                     D.        Carrier shall bear the cost and expense of the furnishing of all fuel, oil, tires and other supplies and
            parts necessary for the safe and lawful operation and maintenance of the equipment used in Carrier’s provision of
            the Services (“Equipment”). Carrier shall not conduct any major Equipment repairs on The Home Depot’s
            property/site/yard. Carrier may conduct minor repairs (e.g. tire changes, preventative maintenance, and light
            changes) on The Home Depot’s property/site/yard where designated by The Home Depot; provided however, such
            repairs shall not occur against or adjacent to any building or structure.

            3.       Bills of Lading and Other Shipping Documents.

                      A.       Each shipment of Products transported hereunder shall be evidenced by a bill of lading or EDI bill
            of lading, which has been approved by The Home Depot, signed by Carrier (including electronic signature if the
            Carrier is technically capable of providing an electronic signature) and showing thereon the kind, quantity, method
            of packaging, and condition of freight received and delivered by Carrier at the loading and unloading points and the
            date and time of the pick-up and delivery. The bill of lading shall constitute evidence that Carrier received the
            shipment in apparent good order and condition unless otherwise noted on the bill of lading. As proof of delivery,
            Carrier shall maintain a permanent record of all bills of lading for a period of not less than two (2) years.

                      B.       All bills of lading, freight receipts and other shipping documents issued by Carrier or any of
            Carrier’s Representatives shall be subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. In the event of a conflict or
            inconsistency between, on the one hand, a bill of lading, freight receipt or other shipping document issued by Carrier
            or Carrier’s Representative and, on the other hand, this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern and control in all
            respects. Any bill of lading, manifest, receipt, form or document used shall be deemed to read as the current
            domestic Uniform Straight Bill of Lading as set forth in the National Motor Freight Classification, Series 100 tariff
            (“NMFC”), provided, however, that no term or condition contained therein shall be deemed to supersede any term or
            condition of this Agreement. Carrier’s driver’s signature on any other shipping document shall be for the purpose of
            acknowledging receipt of the shipment only and the driver’s signature shall not be deemed an acceptance to any
            terms or conditions that vary from this Agreement or those provided in the current NMFC domestic Uniform
            Straight Bill of Lading. Absence or loss of a bill of lading or other receipt form shall not relieve Carrier of
            responsibility for the freight received and accepted by Carrier.

            4.       Use of Subcontractors and Agents

            5.       Lost, Damaged or Destroyed Product

                   Unless otherwise agreed upon by the parties in an SOW, the following terms shall apply to all lost,
            damaged or destroyed Product:

                      A.        The liability of Carrier for the loss or damage to the Products hereunder shall be in accordance
            with the liability imposed by 49 USC 14706; provided however, that no writing of any description, including a filed
            tariff, shall be competent to show that there has been a “shipper waiver” within the meaning of 49 USC 14706(c)
            unless the same shall have been actually signed by a Vice President-Legal of The Home Depot, and provided further
            that The Home Depot shall not be subject to any Carrier limitation of liability unless said limitation is reflected in
            this Master Agreement or an incorporated Statement of Work. Willful misconduct, gross negligence or conversion
            on Carrier’s part or that of its employees, officers, directors, subcontractors or agents shall negate any liability
            limitations which may be contained in this Agreement or any SOW. Carrier’s liability hereunder shall commence
            upon its receipt of the shipment and shall terminate (i) upon delivery of the shipment to the consignee in accordance
            with the governing bill of lading or (ii) upon delivery to the point of origin or such point as instructed by The Home
            Depot if Carrier is unable to deliver a shipment or if consignee refuses a shipment.

                      B.       Except as limited herein, if any shipment hereunder or any part thereof is lost, damaged or
            destroyed while under the care, custody, and/or control of Carrier, Carrier shall pay The Home Depot the
            replacement cost of the Products lost, damaged or destroyed. Notwithstanding the above, The Home Depot and
            Carrier agree and declare that all shipments, including minimum charge shipments, and all commodities transported
            under the conditions of this Agreement shall, regardless of Carrier’s conduct, fault or negligence, be released to a
            value not exceeding $25.00 per pound per package subject to a maximum of $125,000.00 per incident. Carrier’s
            payment obligations shall not be limited or reduced by any released values or released valuations, except as may be
            stated in this Agreement or as expressly agreed in a written document executed by the Vice President-Legal of The
            Home Depot. The replacement cost is hereby defined as the total landed cost of the Product to The Home Depot
            including, without limitation, the manufacturing cost of the merchandise, duty, taxes, transportation charges, storage
            charges, forwarding and brokerage fees.

                      A.        If and to the extent that a party’s performance of any of its obligations under this Agreement is
            directly prevented by a fire, flood, earthquake, elements of nature or acts of God, war or hostilities, terrorism, civil
            insurrection, riots, pandemics that substantially impact Carrier’s ability to perform its services under this Agreement,
            infrastructure disasters, strikes, lockouts or labor disputes, or orders or commands of properly constituted authorities
            (each, a “Force Majeure Event”), and such non-performance could not have been prevented by reasonable
            precautions or preparations by such party, then the non-performing party shall be excused for such non-performance
            of those obligations affected by the Force Majeure Event for as long as such Force Majeure Event continues and
            such party continues to use commercially reasonable efforts to recommence performance whenever and to whatever
            extent possible without delay, including through the use of alternative sources, workaround plans or other business
            contingency plans or means. The party claiming Force Majeure shall notify the other party promptly (but not later
            than twenty-four (24) hours) upon determining that the Force Majeure Event shall affect its performance under this
            Agreement and describe in reasonable detail the nature of the Force Majeure Event. The party claiming Force
            Majeure shall provide notice to the other party within two days after the termination of the Force Majeure Event or
            of such Event’s effect on its performance. The occurrence of a Force Majeure Event shall not limit or otherwise
            affect Carrier’s obligation to implement a business continuity plan or to perform any disaster recovery services. If
            Carrier fails to provide the Services due to the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event in accordance with this
            Agreement, fees payable to Carrier shall be adjusted in such a manner that The Home Depot shall not be liable for
            the payment of any fees for Services that Carrier fails to provide. Nothing in this paragraph shall relieve: (1) Carrier
            from its liability to Shipper for the loss, damage, and/or injury to a shipment transported under this Agreement and
            outlined herein; or, (2) Shipper from its obligation to make payment to Carrier for amounts due and owing under this
            Agreement.

                      B.        If any Force Majeure Event prevents performance of Services by Carrier, The Home Depot may,
            its sole discretion, procure services of similar nature and scope from an alternative source.

                      C.       If any Force Majeure Event persists for ten (10) or more days, The Home Depot shall have the
            right to terminate this Agreement upon ten (10) days written notice to the Carrier.

            performance of this Agreement during such thirty (30) days or for as long as the parties may mutually agree, unless
            and until this Agreement expires or is terminated in accordance with terms specified in this Agreement.

            alteration, disclosure or access, and against all other unlawful activities (the “Provider Security Guidelines”). The
            Provider Security Guidelines shall: (i) include physical, organizational, administrative and technical controls relating
            to the collection, storage, maintenance (including access rights), transmittal and disposal of Home Depot Data, and
            include oversight, tests for vulnerabilities, system checks and measures to prevent and detect unauthorized access; and
            (ii) include, at a minimum (a) a written plan and the development of measures to detect, assess, manage and prevent
            system failures, (b) a regular assessment of internal and external data security risks, including risks to the security,
            confidentiality and integrity of electronic, paper and other records containing Nonpublic Personal Information and
            revision of guidelines to address identified risks, (c) protection of business facilities, paper files, servers, computing
            equipment, including, without limitation all Portable Devices, and backup systems containing Home Depot Data, (d)
            network, application (including databases) and platform security, (e) secure transmission and storage of Nonpublic
            Personal Information, (f) authentication and access control mechanisms over Home Depot Data, media, applications,
            operating systems and equipment, (g) storage limitations such that Home Depot Data resides only on servers and in
            data centers that comply with industry standard data center security controls, and (h) notice and incident response
            procedures. Provider shall ensure that all Provider Personnel are trained in the Provider Security Guidelines and how
            to protect personal information, and shall reasonably discuss the Provider Security Guidelines with Home Depot.
               2.5 Penetration Testing. At least one time each year during the Term of the Agreement, Provider will retain, at
            its sole cost and expense, an independent third party to conduct a penetration test of Provider’s infrastructure designed
            to detect any material security weaknesses in such infrastructure. Provider will use a reputable third party to conduct
            such testing that is certified by recognized industry standards as being qualified to perform such penetration testing.
            Provider will reasonably discuss the results of such testing with Home Depot in a general nature so as not to expose
            any potential vulnerabilities to broader disclosure and, to the extent any such material weakness is found, will take
            appropriate action, prompt under the circumstances, to remedy such weakness. Provider will not engage a third party
            to host Provider’s data or provide Services where Home Depot Data is stored or maintained on such third party’s

          WRM Clean 102920
          20201019                                                       Page 19 of 25
DocuSign Envelope ID: 8F2F3356-0989-48D7-BDE2-2B885C577B13




            servers without requiring such third party to adhere to penetration testing obligations comparable to those contained
            in this section. For the avoidance of doubt, any co-location facility in which Provider leases space, equipment and/or
            power supply from a third party, but Provider maintains control over the use and access of the servers and computers,
            does not constitute a third party hosted server.
               2.6 PCI Compliance. If Provider will have access to or will receive, process, collect, use, store, dispose of, or
            disclose credit, debit or other cardholder payment information, including portions thereof, Provider acknowledges that
            it is responsible for the security of the cardholder data it processes, and hereby represents and warrants that it will
            comply with the most current PCI Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) in connection with the processing of such data,
            including, without limitation: (a) creating and maintaining a secure network to protect cardholder data; (b) using all
            technical and procedural measures reasonably necessary to protect cardholder data it maintains or controls; (c) creating
            and implementing secure measures to limit access to cardholder data; (d) monitoring access to cardholder data it
            maintains or controls; and (e) creating and implementing an information security policy that assures Provider
            Personnel compliance with the foregoing. Provider acknowledges that it is responsible for maintaining compliance
            with the then-current PCI DSS requirements and monitoring the PCI DSS compliance of all Provider Personnel
            provided with access to cardholder data. Provider will provide written documentation satisfactory to Home Depot
            certifying compliance with this section at least annually.
            3.       Requirements for Access to Home Depot’s Systems. In the event Home Depot provides Provider or
            Provider Personnel with access to Home Depot’s Systems, the following terms shall apply:
              3.1 Use. Provider Personnel may not transfer personal or Provider data files or software to Home Depot’s
            Systems, including software that is in the public domain (e.g., shareware or freeware), without prior written consent
            from Home Depot. Any Home Depot equipment used by Provider must be immediately returned to Home Depot upon
            request or if the Agreement is terminated for any reason. Provider agrees to only use remote access software that is
            approved in advance by Home Depot.
               3.2 Access. Provider is granted limited access to only that certain portion of Home Depot’s Systems that it must
            access to perform its obligations and only for so long as such access is necessary. Provider is specifically prohibited
            from accessing any other portion of Home Depot’s Systems. All access to Home Depot’s Systems must originate from
            within the United States unless approved in writing by Home Depot. Provider is not allowed to change the transmission
            process without the prior written approval of Home Depot. Provider Personnel who have access to Home Depot’s
            Systems will: (i) be assigned a unique user ID by Home Depot (“User ID”) and will use only that User ID when
            logging on to Home Depot’s Systems; (ii) log off Home Depot’s Systems immediately upon completion of each
            session of service; (iii) not allow unauthorized individuals to access Home Depot’s Systems; (iv) keep strictly
            confidential the User ID, password and all other information that enables access to Home Depot’s Systems; and (v)
            only utilize such access to perform its obligations to Home Depot. Upon Home Depot’s written request, Provider will
            promptly identify in writing all Provider Personnel who have been granted access to Home Depot’s Systems as of the
            date of the request. Provider acknowledges and agrees that Home Depot owns all information that Provider has access
            to, transmits or obtains via Home Depot’s Systems. Provider will use commercially reasonable security measures for
            its computer systems and information storage facilities which safeguard against the Services provided to Home Depot
            being affected or interrupted.
              3.3 System Administrator. Provider will promptly appoint an employee (a “System Administrator”) who
            will be responsible for: administering Provider’s and Provider Personnel’s access to and use of Home Depot’s
            Systems; changing and deleting User IDs for Provider Personnel who no longer require access to Home Depot’s
            Systems; ensuring Provider’s compliance with these Requirements; collecting and submitting information about
            Provider Personnel with access to Home Depot’s Systems or Home Depot Data; and taking all necessary preventive
            measures to prevent unauthorized access to Home Depot’s Systems. The System Administrator will promptly notify
            Home Depot upon termination of employment or reassignment of Provider Personnel with remote or on-site access to
            Home Depot’s Systems so that User IDs may be changed or deleted and other necessary preventive measures may be

          WRM Clean 102920
          20201019                                                      Page 20 of 25

            taken by Home Depot to prevent unauthorized access. The System Administrator will be Provider’s representative
            with respect to issues with Home Depot’s Systems. Anyone who has been convicted of any felony, or a misdemeanor
            offense related to fraud, identity theft, or computer security, is not allowed to serve as the System Administrator or an
            authorized user with access to Home Depot’s Systems.
              3.4 Passwords. A password will be known only to the user and the System Administrator. There may be no
            sharing of passwords except in an emergency. A compromised password, (e.g., a password that has become known to
            anyone else at any time, including in an emergency) may not be reused. Passwords must be manually entered in order
            to log onto Home Depot’s Systems.
               3.5 Harmful Code. Provider will not introduce any malware, viruses, time or logic bombs, Trojan horses, worms,
            timers, clocks, trap doors, or other computer instructions, devices, or techniques that erase data or programming, infect,
            disrupt, damage, disable, or shut down Home Depot’s Systems or any component of Home Depot’s Systems, including,
            without limitation, its security or data (collectively, “Harmful Code”). In the event Harmful Code is found to have been
            introduced into Home Depot’s Systems by Provider, Provider will, at its sole cost and expense: (a) use commercially
            reasonable efforts to assist Home Depot at Home Depot’s request to mitigate the effects of the Harmful Code; and (b) if
            the Harmful Code causes a loss of operational efficiency or loss of data, mitigate, restore and reimburse such losses. If
            Provider or Provider Personnel discover Harmful Code that may affect Home Depot’s Systems, Provider must report
            it immediately to Home Depot’s Information Systems help desk at (770) 433-8211, ext. 12750.
            4.       Provider Personnel. With respect to any Provider Personnel who have access rights to Home Depot’s
            Systems or Home Depot Data, Provider will: (i) limit such access to only those Provider Personnel with a need for
            such access in order to perform Provider’s obligations under the Agreement; (ii) advise such Provider Personnel (via
            training or other processes designed to acquaint such person with the Provider Security Guidelines and these
            Requirements) prior to providing them with such access rights of the confidential and sensitive nature of such
            information and systems and obligate such Provider Personnel (by contract or otherwise) to abide by the Provider
            Security Guidelines and these Requirements; and (iii) remain responsible for its compliance and the compliance of
            Provider Personnel with these Requirements. Upon Home Depot’s written request, Provider will promptly identify in
            writing all Provider Personnel who have been granted access to any Home Depot Data.
            5.        Changes to Requirements. Home Depot may, from time to time, notify Provider of additional, new or
            updated information privacy and security requirements (“Additional Requirements”) and Provider shall (and for
            clarity, Provider shall ensure Provider Personnel) comply with such Additional Requirements within thirty (30) days
            of receipt of such notice (“Compliance Deadline”). In the event that Provider reasonably believes that it cannot
            comply with such Additional Requirements prior to the Compliance Deadline or otherwise, Provider will promptly
            notify Home Depot prior to the Compliance Deadline and propose an alternative compliance plan for Home Depot’s
            consideration. If the parties cannot mutually agree on an alternative compliance plan prior to the original Compliance
            Deadline (or any extension thereto approved in writing by Home Depot), Home Depot, in its sole discretion, will have
            the right to immediately terminate the Agreement or the relevant SOW, in whole or in part, without penalty. The Basic
            Requirements and Additional Requirements are collectively referred to as (“Requirements”). Provider and Provider
            Personnel shall comply with these Requirements at all times during the Term of the Agreement and thereafter until
            such time as they each no longer have possession of Home Depot Data or access to Home Depot’s Systems. The acts
            or omissions of Provider Personnel or Provider’s Affiliates (and such Affiliates’ employees, agents, representatives,
            contractors or subcontractors) will also be deemed the acts or omissions of Provider.
            6.      Monitoring. Home Depot may periodically monitor, and/or review after the fact, Provider’s use of Home
            Depot’s Systems, Home Depot Data, and any other technology owned, licensed or leased by Home Depot. Home
            Depot or its representatives have the right to review Provider’s and Provider Personnel’s compliance with these
            Requirements during normal business hours. Such reviews will be conducted at mutually-convenient times, in a
            manner that does not materially disrupt Provider’s business operations. If, as a result of such review, Home Depot
            determines that Provider is not in compliance with these Requirements, it will notify Provider of such non-compliance

            7.        Security Incident. If Provider discovers or is notified of any (i) unauthorized acquisition, destruction, loss,
            alteration of or access to Home Depot Data, or (ii) breach or potential breach of security relating to Home Depot Data
            or Home Depot’s Systems (each a “Security Incident”), Provider will immediately: (a) notify Home Depot’s
            Information Systems help desk at (770) 433-8211 ext. 12750, and the applicable Home Depot contact at the address
            specified in the Notices section of the Agreement of such Security Incident and by email or phone, but in no case later
            than 24 hours after Provider has become aware of the Security Incident; and (b) if the applicable Home Depot Data was
            in the possession of Provider at the time of such Security Incident, Provider shall: (1) start an investigation of the Security
            Incident and take all appropriate actions to remediate the effects of the Security Incident and mitigate any risks that
            may arise from the Security Incident; (2) provide Home Depot with timely and ongoing reports on the outcome of its
            investigation including any risk to Home Depot Data, the corrective action Provider will take, or has taken, to respond
            to the Security Incident and such other information as Home Depot may reasonably request; (3) ensure that all risks
            associated with such Security Incident are ultimately resolved within thirty (30) days of such Security Incident; (4)
            preserve all records and other evidence relating to the Security Incident; and (5) provide Home Depot with assurances
            reasonably satisfactory to Home Depot that such Security Incident shall not reoccur. Home Depot may disclose the
            occurrence of a Security Incident involving Nonpublic Personal Information in connection with notice to Home
            Depot’s customers, employees or vendors, including both past and prospective customers, employees and vendors,
            governmental authorities, law enforcement agencies, or any other notice required by law or deemed necessary or
            prudent in Home Depot’s sole discretion, including, as applicable any substitute notice required by law
            (“Notifications”). Provider shall cooperate in good faith with Home Depot in Home Depot’s handling of any Security
            Incident, including, without limitation any investigation, reporting, the timing and manner of any Notifications, or
            other obligations required by applicable law or regulation, or as otherwise required by Home Depot to respond to and
            mitigate any damages caused by the Security Incident. Provider agrees to reimburse Home Depot for any fines, costs
            and losses incurred in connection with a Security Incident, including, without limitation, the cost of reconstructing
            data and data forensics (including any security audits or reviews of Provider’s systems reasonably requested by Home
            Depot), the cost of Notifications (including call center support services) and providing identity theft monitoring and
            resolution services (including credit monitoring services) to affected parties, and any reasonable outside counsel fees
            incurred by Home Depot related to such Security Incident. Provider will promptly designate an employee familiar
            with Provider’s obligations pursuant to these Requirements to act as Home Depot’s primary contact for questions it
            may have or assistance it may require related to a Security Incident (including Home Depot’s internal investigation of
            a Security Incident) or Provider’s compliance with these Requirements (“Provider Contact”). The Provider Contact
            will promptly respond to all such Home Depot requests. Provider will ensure that Home Depot has at all times the
            most current contact information for the Provider Contact, which shall include at a minimum, Name, Title, Phone
            Number, Emergency Phone Number, and Email Address.

                                        PROHIBITED AND EXCLUDED COMMODITIES

            Unless otherwise provided the following commodities will not be accepted for shipment:
               • Articles of extraordinary value
               • Single handling units greater than 27’
               • Asbestos friable (crumbly)
               • Bank bills
               • Biological products
               • Blood, blood related components and blood related products
               • Business records-current or archived
               • Carbon black (NOTE: See item 1)
               • Cigarettes and cigars (Exceptions to be made for RETL customers within the RETL footprint)
               • Coins
               • Collectibles, other than new
               • Commodities – unpackaged bulk commodities
               • Corpses
               • Cream, fresh
               • Cultures of Etiologic agents
               • Currency
               • Deeds
               • Diagnostic specimens
               • Drafts
               • Envelopes or wrappers, government stamped, in shipments weighing 30,000 pounds or more
               • Etiologic agents / Infectious Substances (Division 6.2)

               • Explosives, Mexico – (All Classes & divisions)

                                           AMENDMENT TO
                   FOR LESS-THAN-TRUCKLOAD (LTL) TRANSPORTATION
 This AMENDMENT dated October 27th, 2022, (Amendment) is attached to and made part of the Master
Logistics Services Agreement dated as of November 7th, 2020 (the “Agreement”) by and between YRC
Inc. d/b/a YRC Freight, a Delaware corporation; USF Holland LLC, d/b/a Holland, a Delaware limited
liability company; USF Reddaway Inc. d/b/a Reddaway, an Oregon corporation; and New Penn Motor
Express LLC, d/b/a New Penn Motor Express a Delaware limited liability (the “YRC Carriers”) (who
enter into this Statement of Work through their authorized agent, YRC Enterprise Services, Inc., a
Delaware corporation) (“Carrier”) and Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., on behalf of itself and its Affiliates
(collectively, “The Home Depot”). Affiliates may be added or deleted from this Agreement by written
agreement of the Parties.
WHEREAS, Carrier and Home Depot desire amend the Master Logistics Services Agreement
(“Agreement”) making the following changes.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual agreement hereinafter contained, the receipt and
sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties agree that the Agreement shall be and hereby is
amended as follows:



1) With regard to each trailer that is dropped off at any Home Depot facility in connection with Carrier
   providing Services under this Agreement, Home Depot may, at its discretion, when loading trailers
   dropped off by Carrier, insert GPS tracking devices for tracking the location of the trailer into boxes
   or cartons loaded by Home Depot.


2) Access to Drop Lots. During such times as Carrier accesses certain property in which Home Depot
   has a property interest and is used for the storing, collection, or interchanging of trailers (“Drop Lot”
   or “Drop Lots”) to access, operate, or otherwise manage Carrier’s trailers, Carrier agrees to the
   following terms and conditions (These Drop Lots shall be inclusive of such lots located at or adjacent
   to Home Depot Distribution Centers, as well as lots or spaces located remote to the Distribution
   Centers, but utilized to drop off temporarily store and pick-up trailers for the benefit of Distribution
   Center operations)

        (a)      Home Depot will allow Carrier to access Drop Lots for the sole purpose of providing
    Services to Home Depot pursuant to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. Carrier
    acknowledges and agrees that its access to Drop Lots is limited to the areas and times necessary to
    perform its activities and the Services.

        (b)      Carrier accepts and agrees that it shall perform all activities or Services on Drop Lots in
    compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations, including, but not limited
    to having all required licenses, permits and insurance and complying with all required safety
    practices, including but not limited to, those posted by Home Depot.




                                                INTERNAL USE
    (c)      Carrier shall furnish, at its own expense and at its sole and exclusive risk of loss or
damage, the equipment, supplies, and other materials used to perform any activities or Services on the
Drop Lots. Carrier shall assume full responsibility for the acts and omissions of its employees,
officers, agents, representatives, subcontractors, and other persons employed or retained in connection
with the performance of its activities or Services on the Drop Lots.

    (d)       Carrier accepts and agrees: (i) that Carrier enters the Drop Lots and performs its activities
or Services thereon at its own risk; (ii) that Home Depot shall bear no liability to Carrier or third-
parties, in any event, arising out of or related to performance of Carrier’s activities or presence on the
Drop Lots absent Home Depot’s gross negligence or willful misconduct; (iii) that Home Depot shall
bear no liability to Carrier or third-parties regarding the presence or absence of any safety features of
the Drop Lots, including but not limited to, proper lighting, staffing with security personnel, gating,
fencing, or recording of activity on the Drop Lots by Closed-Circuit Television or other electronic
means; and (iv) Home Depot shall bear no liability whatsoever for special, indirect or consequential
damages, regardless of foreseeability.


    (e)      Home Depot may issue and post rules or procedures in or around Drop Lots applicable to
Carrier’s activities on the Drop Lots. Carrier accepts and agrees that it will comply with all posted
rules or other notifications regarding prohibited or permissive activities on the Drop Lots as
applicable. Carrier agrees that the Distribution Center Safety Compliance operating requirement, as
outlined in the attached Exhibit B, shall, without limitation, govern Carrier’s activities on the Drop
Lot and Carrier agrees to comply with such requirements while on the Drop Lot.

    (f)      Carrier hereby grants Home Depot permission to access and use of Carrier’s trailers
while stored on Drop Lots for the purpose of moving the trailers into, within, or off of the Drop Lot,
as required in Home Depot’s sole discretion. Carrier shall not be responsible for damage to person or
property arising out of Home Depot’s access to Carrier’s trailers in the Drop Lot.

    (g)     Carrier accepts and agrees to promptly notify Home Depot in the event Carrier is
involved in or aware of any loss or damage to person or property caused, allegedly, caused, or in any
way arising out of Carrier’s performance of activities or Services on the Drop Lots.

     (h)       Carrier agrees that it shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Home Depot, including
its affiliates, subsidiaries, associates, officers and agents, from and against any and all claims,
lawsuits, judgments, losses, civil penalties, actions (administrative or judicial), liabilities, damages,
fines, costs (including environmental remediation), and expenses (including reasonable attorney’s
fees) incurred or to be incurred, and which may be made or are brought against Home Depot by any
individual, person (including but not limited to, Carrier’s employees, agents, representatives,
contractors and assigns), corporation, government, governmental agency, class, or any other entity
whatsoever, arising out of or alleged to have arisen out of: (a) injury or death to person or damage to
property caused, allegedly caused, or in any way arising out of Carrier’s performance of activities or
Services on the Drop Lots except to the extent any claims are caused by the gross negligence or
willful misconduct of Home Depot; and (b) violation of any federal, state or local law, rule, regulation
or ordinance governing Carrier’s activities including as it accesses the Drop Lots. Carrier’s
obligations under this Section shall not be limited by the insurance required under this Agreement.

      previous Amendments shall remain in full force and effect.

                                             GENERAL CARRIER EDI REQUIREMENTS



            The following EDI specific requirements will apply to all business entities and segments herein this document.



            The following EDI specific requirements will not apply unless and until implementation of EDI in this
            operation is completed.



                                                           EDI SSM Compliance

                                             AF             Ship Date (Arrived at Origin Terminal)

                                             AG                     Estimated Arrival Date

                                             AV                Shipment Available for Delivery

                                            D1/S1            Delivery Date (Departed at Delivery)



            SSM On-Time – Carrier should transmit 4 SSM statuses and on-time. Carrier is expected to provide 98.5%
            compliance.



            EDI Standards – For loads originating at a Home Depot supplier, carrier will provide timely electronic load status
            updates as follows:

                                             STATEMENT OF WORK
                                                    FOR
                                  LESS-THAN-TRUCKLOAD (LTL) TRANSPORTATION


                      This Statement of Work (“SOW”) is dated as of October 27th, 2022 (“Effective Date”), and is
            attached to and made a part of the Master Logistics Services Agreement dated as of November 7th, 2020
            (the “Agreement”) by and between YRC Inc. d/b/a YRC Freight, a Delaware corporation; USF Holland
            LLC, d/b/a Holland, a Delaware limited liability company; USF Reddaway Inc. d/b/a Reddaway, an Oregon
            corporation; and New Penn Motor Express LLC, d/b/a New Penn Motor Express a Delaware limited
            liability (the “YRC Carriers”) (who enter into this Statement of Work through their authorized agent, YRC
            Enterprise Services, Inc., a Delaware corporation) (“Carrier”) and Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., on behalf of
            itself and its Affiliates (collectively, “The Home Depot”).

                    NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the terms and conditions set forth herein, the parties agree
            as follows:

            1. TERM: This SOW is effective from October 27th, 2022 (“Commencement Date”) through October 27th,
               2023 (“Termination Date”), unless earlier terminated pursuant to the terms of the Agreement.

            2. BUSINESS SEGMENT DEFINITIONS:
                    a. First Mile – Inclusive of inbound operations, originating at Vendor locations and delivering
                        to Home Depot stores and/or distribution centers.
                    b. Middle Mile – Inclusive of middle mile operations, originating at Home Depot Vendor
                        locations, Home Depot stores and/or distribution centers and delivering to Home Depot third-
                        party delivery agents, Home Depot stores and/or distribution centers.
                    c. Last Mile – Inclusive of vendor direct freight, originating from Vendor locations to customer
                        residences.

            3. SERVICES: Carrier will provide the following general services:

                        a. Transport freight as a qualified motor contract carrier in interstate and/or intrastate commerce
                           and furnish motor contract carrier services to Home Depot as Home Depot may from time-
                           to-time request.
                        b. When service is requested by The Home Depot to a destination not served directly by Carrier,
                           Carrier shall serve as The Home Depot’s agent and deliver the shipment to the final
                           destination based on the LTL Carrier designated by The Home Depot routing guide (a “Core
                           Carrier”).
                                  1.Core Carrier is required to service all zip codes within the state to state pairs awarded.
                                  2.Core Carrier is required to provide electronic updates through final delivery even if
                                     interlined or subcontracted.
                                  3.Core Carrier is required to service all volume within their awarded lanes.
                        c. When Carrier interlines with a non-core carrier (non-contracted), all charges will be paid
                           based on the pricing program of the origin Carrier. In such instances, the non-core carrier
                           shall be considered an agent of Carrier and Carrier shall remain liable to The Home Depot
                           for cargo loss, damage or delay to the same extent as if Carrier performed the services
                           directly.
                        d. In any situation, Carrier shall be listed on the bill of lading.

            4. PAYMENT AND INVOICING:
                   a. As full compensation for the Services provided by Carrier hereunder, The Home Depot shall
                      pay Carrier in accordance the terms set forth in Schedule A, Schedule B, and any specific
                      pricing schedule (“Pricing Schedule”) executed by the parties which are incorporated hereto
                      by reference and made a part of this SOW.
                   b. Carrier shall invoice The Home Depot promptly following completion of each shipment.
                      Each invoice shall be prepared in accordance with The Home Depot freight bill requirements
                      set forth herein as Schedule E and each undisputed invoice shall be payable by The Home
                      Depot within forty-five (45) days after receipt by The Home Depot. The Home Depot shall
                      have no obligation to pay any invoice that is not timely presented and, except as provided in
                      Section 3c of this SOW with respect to revised invoices, Carrier hereby waives any right to
                      collect from The Home Depot for any original invoice that is not presented within ninety (90)
                      days from the date of delivery of the shipment to which the invoice pertains.
                   c. Carrier shall have ninety (90) days from the date of the delivery of a shipment to present any
                      revised invoice for charges additional to those initially invoiced for said shipment.
                   d. The Home Depot shall refuse payment and not pay for any services, additional charges or
                      other fees invoiced by Carrier, which do not comply with The Home Depot’s documentation
                      requirements as outlined in Schedule E, attached hereto and made a part hereof.
                   e. Carrier shall provide The Home Depot with at least sixty (60) days prior written notice to
                      request a pricing review. Other than expressly provided for under this SOW or agreed to in
                      writing by The Home Depot, no tariffs shall apply with respect to the shipments transported
                      by Carrier under this Agreement, and no other tariffs are incorporated herein by reference.
                   f. All additional charges and accessorial services, including but not limited to exclusive vehicle
                      use, reconsignment, redelivery, stop-offs in-transit, product storage, product
                      sorting/segregation, pallet exchanges, protective services, additional labor for
                      loading/unloading, notification prior to delivery, and linehaul rates shall be provided at the
                      prices set forth on Application of Governing Rules, which is attached hereto as Schedule B
                      and made a part hereof.
                   g. All mileages for truckload shipments shall be determined in accordance with PC*Miler,
                      Version 30.0 Worldwide, “Shortest Route,” “Borders Open” unless specifically otherwise
                      agreed to by the parties. Should The Home Depot update from the current version, Carrier
                      may be required to update to the prescribed version within sixty (60) days of notification.
                      All mile charges on freight bills are audited using PC*Miler, Version 30.0 Worldwide,
                      “Shortest Route,” “Borders Open.”
                   h. The Home Depot shall specify whether the charges for any shipment hereunder shall be
                      prepaid or collect.

            5. SCHEDULING AND DELIVERY:
                    a. All appointments for pick-up and delivery must be scheduled at least twenty-four (24) hours
                       prior to said pick-up and delivery unless written authorization to the contrary is received from
                       The Home Depot. All appointments for pick-up from THD’s DFC locations must occur
                       within 30 minutes of the established critical pull time.
                    b. All loading of freight must be done in the presence of the Carrier, unless mutually agreed
                       upon by Carrier and the applicable consignor (“Consignor”) that the Consignor will provide
                       a bill of lading receipt annotated as “Shipper’s Load and Count”; provided, however, that
                       where the Consignor does not agree to provide a bill of lading receipt annotated as “Shipper’s
                       Load and Count,” Carrier must issue a bill of lading receipt for the count and condition of
                       the load and such bill of lading receipt will serve as evidence of the count and condition at
                       origin. All unloading of freight must be done in the presence of Carrier, unless otherwise
                       mutually agreed upon by Carrier and The Home Depot in writing prior to delivery. In the

            7. ADDITIONAL TERMS REGARDING DAMAGED OR DEFECTIVE PRODUCTS:
                    a. Notwithstanding any other term to the contrary in the Agreement, Carrier’s maximum
                       liability for loss and damage of Products is $125,000.00 per load.
                    b. If any Products delivered to The Home Depot by Carrier are rejected by The Home Depot
                       for being damaged or defective as determined by The Home Depot, Carrier agrees to follow
                       the procedures set forth below:
                               1.Regarding rejected Products bearing any of The Home Depot trademarks or private
                                 labels set forth on Schedule G hereto (“The Home Depot Brands and Private
                                 Labels”), Carrier shall immediately notify the supplier as to the type and quantity of
                                 such Products to obtain return authority and applicable return authorization.
                               2.Regarding rejected Products that are not The Home Depot Brands and Private
                                 Labels, Carrier shall immediately notify the supplier as to the type and quantity of
                                 such Products to obtain return authority and applicable return authorization.
                               3.Carrier shall not salvage, sell or dispose of any Products that are The Home Depot
                                 Brands or Private Labels as set forth on Schedule G. Home Depot agrees to mitigate
                                 cargo claims on these returns to the lowest extent possible. The Home Depot agrees
                                 to at least provide Carrier a fifty percent (50%) salvage allowance on these claims
                                 which will be credited to Carrier. The Home Depot reserves the right to determine
                                 disposition of the returned freight without prejudice to any claim it may have against
                                 Carrier.
                               4.The Home Depot reserves the right to update and amend Schedule G from time to
                                 time, subject to fifteen (15) days prior written notice to Carrier; provided, however,
                                 with respect to new Home Depot Brands and Private Labels that Carrier has
                                 knowledge of but are not yet listed on Schedule G, Carrier shall comply with the
                                 obligations set forth herein. All questions and inquiries related to the matters set
                                 forth in this Section shall be addressed to Manager of Logistics (LTL Operations) or
                                 Manager of Logistics (LTL Strategy) of The Home Depot.

                        d. All claims for a concealed loss or concealed damage, provided there is no visible evidence

                                                                    SCHEDULE A
                                                                   PRICING TERMS

            Tariff and Year: All ratings and discounts will be based on the The Home Depot customized Czarlite International Tariff,
            effective 8/29/05 for domestic shipments, and determined by Canada Lite, effective 5/2/2005, for shipments into or out of Canada.

            Interline Pricing: If a point is not served directly, carrier must interline with THD Routing Guide specified Core Carrier for the
            Destination State, rates and discounts for said shipments will reflect min/discounts detailed in Schedule A-7.

            Freight Classification: Except as noted below, all Inbound and Outbound HD Supply and Home Depot collect, and third-party
            billing shipments will be rated based on the tiered FAK structure specified.

            FAK Tier Structures:
                    Inbound/Outbound HD Supply and Home Depot:
                    Tier 1 – FAK 55 (Classes 50-60)
                    Tier 2 – FAK 70 (Classes 65-85)
                    Tier 3 – FAK 100 (Classes 92.5-150)
                    Tier 4 – FAK 250 (Classes 175-500)


            For outbound prepaid and collect shipments when The Home Depot is the debtor, shipments will be rated off an FAK class rating
            of 70, except for shipments originating from locations found on FAK Vendor Exception List located in Schedule A. For outbound
            prepaid and outbound collect shipments originating from locations found on FAK Vendor Exception List located in Schedule A-1,
            shipments will be rated based on the tiered FAK structure specified. Actual class will apply on outbound shipments when Home
            Depot is not the debtor.

            All FAK Vendor exceptions will be rated at set FAK tier based on the FAK Vendor exception list specified in the Schedule A.
            Any FAK Vendor change must be approved by THD and move from one tier to another for an exception to be granted.

            Truckload Shipments: Shipments weighing less than or equal to 10,000-pounds will be rated at the lowest applicable rate as
            determined by Home Depot customized Czarlite International Tariff, effective 8/29/05 for domestic shipments, and determined
            by Canada Lite, effective 5/2/2005, for shipments into or out of Canada. Shipments exceeding 10,000 pounds will take a 10,000-
            pound line of rates with applicable discount as determined by The Home Depot customized Czarlite International Tariff,
            effective 8/29/05 for domestic shipments, and determined by Canada Lite, effective 5/2/2005 for shipments into or out of Canada.

            Incentive Pricing: Rates may be established or amended in writing in order to meet The Home Depot’s specialized and distinct
            needs. Carrier shall immediately confirm any such change by a signed amendment or addendum sent to The Home Depot and said
            change shall be signed by The Home Depot and returned to Carrier as confirmation of The Home Depot’s agreement. All such
            fully executed amendments or addendums shall be attached to this Agreement and shall become a part hereof.

            Conflicting rates: In the case where there is a conflict among or between rates of different rate types, the applicable rate will be
            determined as follows:
                     Point to point rates will take precedence over all other rates.
                     Zip to zip rates will take precedence over all other rates except point to point rates.
                     Point to State rates will take precedence over state to state rates.
                     State to state rates will apply only when there is no applicable point to point rate, no applicable zip to zip rate and no
                      applicable point to state rate.
                     Country to country rates will apply only there is no applicable state to state rate, no applicable point to point rate, no
                      applicable zip to zip rate and no applicable point to state rate.

            Lane Characteristics Changes: When the characteristics of the lane change, from the date of identification, The Home Depot
            and Carrier will have sixty (60) days to analyze and renegotiate the pricing of the lane. The Home Depot reserves the right to rebid
            lanes where the characteristics have changed due to volume, commodity, new store location, new vendors, etc.

            In the case where there is a conflict among or between rates of the same rate type, the lower rate will apply.

            Discounts and Minimum Charges: Reference Schedule A-1

                    Where the carrier and Home Depot have agreed to spot load trailers at a Home Depot facility, the Home Depot has 5
                    days free time to unload, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays.

                    For trailers spotted before noon, free time commences on the day the trailer is spotted.

                    For trailers spotted after noon, free time commences on the day following the day the trailer is spotted.
                    Upon expiration of free time, including Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays the charges below will apply.

                    Detention of Carrier’s Vehicle at Origin, Without Power:
                                                                                                                   WAIVED
                    Where Carrier and Home Depot have agreed to spot empty trailers at a Home Depot facility or at a Home Depot vendor
                    facility, such spotted trailers will be considered a “trailer pool,” and no detention shall apply to individual trailers.

                    Pickups With Power Unit:
                                                                                                               2 hours free time
                                                                                                               $1.00 per minute

                    Pickup appointments are to be scheduled as required by the shipping facility policy. For each pickup stop, free time
                    will be 2 hours. Time starts from the scheduled pickup appointment time or check-in with shipping personnel,
                    whichever comes later. Upon arrival and check-in with shipping personnel, Carriers more than 15 minutes late for a
                    scheduled pickup appointment cannot charge detention. Charges will start after the expiration of free time. Detention
                    with power unit will be charged at the rate of $1.00 per minute, billed by the minute.

                    Detention charges incurred at Home Depot vendor sites are the responsibility of Home Depot.

                    Home Depot will agree to accept and process Detention Claims by Carrier and pay for any such claims accordingly
                    ONLY if the arrival and departure status messages (“ssms”) are validated for the Carrier’s claim. Carriers should
                    contact the Home Depot Inbound Manager if they are experiencing consistent delays with a vendor.



                     Deliveries With Power Unit (THD Facilities Only):
                                                                                                               2 hours free time
                                                                                                               $1.00 per minute

                     For each delivery stop, free time will be 2 hours. Time starts from the scheduled appointment time or check-in with
                     receiving, whichever comes later. Upon arrival and check-in with receiving personnel, Carriers more than 15 minutes
                     late for a scheduled delivery appointment cannot charge detention. Charges will start after the expiration of free time.
                     Detention with power unit will be charged at the rate of $1.00 per minute, billed by the minute.

                     All deliveries to Home Depot facilities require a delivery appointment made at least 24 hours in advance of the
                     anticipated time of delivery.

                     Carrier will notify Home Depot by email, either Store Manager or DC Manager or Transportation Planner that routes
                     the particular load, prior to the commencement of detention charges that such charges will begin accruing.

                    Trailer Dwell/Detention without power:
                    Charges $200 or more require approval from the DC Transportation Managers. This would also include any DC or
                    Operations Managers on-site. For escalation, Carrier will notify Home Depot by email, either Store Manager or DC
                    Manager or Transportation Planner that routes the particular load, prior to the commencement of detention charges that
                    such charges will begin accruing. Carrier can reference either their Transportation Service Agreement or Broker
                    Transportation Service Agreement.
